findings.description: The `Signature` describe block only exercises successful decodes (fully-populated, minimal, open `meaning`, round-trip). It never asserts that `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(Signature)` fails on a missing required field (`signerId`, `meaning`, `signedAt`) or a wrong-typed one (e.g. `signedAt` as a string). `Signature.ts`'s own doc comment (lines 6-13) states it meets the same ADR-QD-002 trust-boundary condition as `Policy`/`Obligation` — and `Policy.test.ts` (e.g. "the Obligation schema rejects a malformed payload via decode", line 123) does cover exactly this class of negative case for its own struct schemas. `Signature` is the one Schema-derived type in this sweep's scope with zero decode-failure coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test (or a few) asserting `Effect.result(Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(Signature)(...))` is a Failure for a payload missing `signerId`/`meaning`/`signedAt` and for one with a wrong-typed field (e.g. `signedAt: "now"`).
